ru: не было бы счастья, да несчастье помогло
definition: Something that seems bad initially but ultimately has a positive result.
examples: Losing that job turned out to be a blessing in disguise.

ru: зануда, тот, кто портит всем настроение; облом
definition: Someone or something that spoils other people's enjoyment or excitement.
examples: Don't be a buzzkill — we're just celebrating.

term: a hell of a lot (of something)
ru: чертовски много, до хрена, гораздо (перед сравнительной степенью)
definition: An extremely large amount or quantity of something.
examples: We spent a hell of a lot of time fixing the problem.

ru: линия взгляда / прямая видимость, поле зрения
definition: A clear, unobstructed path between an observer and what they can see.
examples: The trees blocked our line of sight to the entrance.

ru: ощущение смысла, чувство цели (понимание, ради чего ты что-то делаешь)
definition: The feeling that your actions have meaning and a clear goal.
examples: Volunteering gave her a renewed sense of purpose.

definition: During the days at the end of the working week, either generally or on a particular occasion.
examples: I usually go hiking at weekends.
note: Common in British English; American usage often on weekends / on the weekend.

ru: если бы не; если бы не кто-то / что-то; без (кого-то / чего-то)
definition: If it had not been for a particular person or thing.
examples: But for your help, we would have missed the deadline.

term: in for a penny, in for a pound
ipa: /ˌɪn fər ə ˈpeni ˌɪn fər ə ˈpaʊnd/
ru: сказал «а» — говори «б»; взялся за гуж — не говори, что не дюж; гулять так гулять
definition: Once committed to something, you should see it through even if it becomes difficult.
examples: We've started the renovation; in for a penny, in for a pound.

definition: Briefly or casually, without giving something much attention.
examples: She mentioned the vacancy in passing.

definition: In the part of a picture or scene closest to the viewer.
examples: A cyclist appears in the foreground of the photograph.

term: on the decline / on the wane
definition: Becoming less common, strong, popular or successful.
examples: Demand for the product is on the decline.

definition: People in general rather than the wealthy, famous or powerful.
examples: The policy will affect ordinary people most.

definition: So costly that paying for it is practically impossible or unreasonable.
examples: Housing in the city centre is prohibitively expensive.

definition: Slightly fat, especially with a soft, rounded appearance.
examples: The puppy had a pudgy little belly.

definition: The part of a seat that supports a person's back.
examples: He hung his jacket over the back of a chair.

ru: привлекать, нравиться кому-то. That's what appeals to me most — именно это мне больше всего нравится.
definition: To attract or interest a person; to seem enjoyable or desirable to them.
examples: The chance to work independently really appeals to me.

ru: это надолго, пришло всерьёз и навсегда
definition: To have become a lasting part of life rather than a temporary trend.
examples: Remote work looks as though it's here to stay.

term: to blur the line(s) between X and Y
ru: стирать / размывать грань между X и Y
definition: To make the distinction between two things less clear.
examples: AI can blur the line between human and machine-generated content.

term: to come as a surprise (to someone)
definition: To be unexpected or cause someone to feel surprised.
examples: The decision came as a surprise to everyone.

term: to get the hang of something
definition: To learn how to do something through practice and become comfortable with it.
examples: I'm finally getting the hang of the new software.

term: to play a role in something
definition: To have an influence or function in a process or situation.
examples: Trust plays a crucial role in negotiations.

term: to pose a risk to something / someone
definition: To create the possibility of harm or danger for someone or something.
examples: The delay could pose a risk to patient safety.

ru: 1) основываться на, зависеть от, держаться на; 2) лежать / опираться на; (о взгляде) остановиться на
definition: To depend on or be based on a particular fact, principle or condition.
examples: The whole argument rests on a questionable assumption.

term: to show no sign(s) of slowing down
ru: не собирается замедляться, не сбавляет темп
definition: To continue at a fast rate without any indication of becoming slower.
examples: The company shows no signs of slowing down.

definition: To speak about someone or something with enthusiastic approval.
examples: Her former colleagues keep singing her praises.

definition: To tell people about a potential danger or unwanted development.
examples: Experts warned of further disruption.

term: would love it if … (I'd love it if …)
ru: Я был бы очень рад, если бы... / Мне бы очень хотелось, чтобы...
definition: To strongly wish for a particular event or situation to happen.
examples: I'd love it if we could finish early today.

definition: A continuing increase in how quickly something is growing or changing.
examples: The report found a sustained acceleration in productivity growth.

definition: The first assessment of the monetary worth of a business or asset.
examples: The initial valuation was lower than investors expected.

term: at a fraction of the cost
ru: за малую долю стоимости, в разы дешевле
definition: For a much smaller share of the usual or expected price.
examples: The software provides similar features at a fraction of the cost.

ru: в целом, взвесив все за и против; в итоге
definition: Considering all the advantages and disadvantages together.
examples: On balance, the benefits outweigh the risks.

definition: The arguments and evidence supporting a particular proposal or position.
examples: She made a convincing case for reform.

ru: подать заявку / откликнуться на вакансию, устраиваться на работу
definition: To submit an application to be considered for employment.
examples: I applied for a job at a technology company.
note: Apply for a position, but apply to a company.

ru: подать заявку в компанию, обратиться в компанию (на работу)
definition: To send an application to an organisation, especially seeking employment.
examples: She applied to several companies before getting an interview.

definition: To investigate a business or transaction carefully before a major decision.
examples: The buyer carried out due diligence before the acquisition.

ru: последовать примеру, сделать то же самое
definition: To do the same thing that another person or organisation has just done.
examples: One bank reduced its fees, and others followed suit.

term: to harness the strengths of something
definition: To make effective use of the advantages or abilities of something.
examples: The team needs to harness the strengths of both approaches.

term: to keep a firm grip on something
definition: To maintain strong control over a situation or activity.
examples: The manager kept a firm grip on spending.

term: to laud the benefits of something
definition: To praise the positive effects or advantages of something enthusiastically.
examples: Executives lauded the benefits of the new system.

term: to make significant inroads into something
ru: значительно продвинуться, заметно потеснить, проникнуть (на рынок, в сферу)
definition: To achieve substantial progress in an area or gain share in a market.
examples: The company made significant inroads into the European market.

definition: To invest large amounts of money in a project or activity.
examples: The firm is ploughing cash into research.

ru: вызывать серьёзные опасения; поднимать серьёзные вопросы
definition: To cause significant worry or bring important problems to public attention.
examples: The proposal raised serious concerns about privacy.

definition: To continue being responsible and answerable for something.
examples: Senior managers remain accountable for the decision.

definition: To hurry and work hard to reach the level of someone who is ahead.
examples: Smaller firms are scrambling to catch up.

definition: To make brief contact with someone to exchange updates or coordinate.
examples: Let's touch base after the meeting.
note: Informal business English; touch base with someone.

definition: A system that enables direct communication between the brain and an electronic device.
examples: Researchers developed a brain–computer interface for communication.

definition: A substantial amount of freedom to act or make decisions independently.
examples: The robot operates with a high degree of autonomy.

definition: A military underwater vessel powered by a nuclear reactor.
examples: A nuclear submarine can remain submerged for long periods.
note: Nuclear refers to propulsion, not necessarily to weapons.

definition: To put artificial-intelligence applications into practical use.
examples: The firm deployed AI tools to review contracts.

definition: To accept and actively adopt recently developed technical methods or devices.
examples: Smaller businesses are starting to embrace new technology.

definition: To make a process happen much faster to a substantial degree.
examples: Better computing power could profoundly accelerate discovery.

term: to train on vast amounts of data
definition: To develop a model using extremely large datasets as training material.
examples: The system was trained on vast amounts of data.
note: An AI model is trained on data; people train with materials.

definition: A hospital room specially equipped for surgical operations.
examples: The patient was taken to the operating theatre.

definition: A rubber-coated weight disc designed to be safely dropped during lifting.
examples: Use a bumper plate when practising Olympic lifts.

definition: To put weight plates onto a barbell before an exercise.
examples: Load the bar with another ten kilos.

definition: To increase the speed or intensity of an activity or competition.
examples: The runners pushed the pace in the final kilometre.

definition: A legal requirement to make specified information available to others.
examples: The regulations impose mandatory disclosure of certain risks.

definition: To be at risk of formal punishment at work for breaking rules.
examples: An employee may face disciplinary action for serious misconduct.

term: to prompt regulators to step in
definition: To cause government supervisors to intervene in a situation.
examples: The incident prompted regulators to step in.

definition: For a dispute or case to come before a court for consideration.
examples: The dispute eventually reached court.
note: Also common: the case went to court.

definition: To weaken people's confidence in institutions or authorities.
examples: The scandal undermined public trust in the regulator.

definition: To make courts and legal remedies more accessible to people.
examples: The reforms aim to widen access to justice.

definition: A sudden, sharp feeling of embarrassment or guilt.
examples: She felt a pang of shame when she remembered what she had said.
note: Common: to feel a pang of shame; also a pang of guilt / regret.

definition: To spend time and energy trying to achieve or improve something.
examples: She put a lot of effort into improving her English.

definition: To turn out or develop in a particular way.
examples: Things did not pan out as we had hoped.

term: to be reluctant to do something
definition: To feel hesitant or unwilling to do something.
examples: He was reluctant to accept the offer.
note: be reluctant to + infinitive; it does not necessarily mean refusal.

definition: To deal with distressing psychological consequences after an event.
examples: She faced the emotional fallout of losing her job.
note: In a specific context, often: face the emotional fallout of/from something.

definition: To set aside pride to do something necessary but uncomfortable.
examples: He swallowed his pride and apologised.

definition: To change your focus or approach to something.
examples: Let’s switch gears and discuss the budget.
note: Especially common in American English; British change gear is also used.

definition: To reach an agreement with someone, usually after negotiation, with benefits or concessions for both sides.
examples: After lengthy negotiations, the two companies finally struck a bargain.
We struck a bargain: I would handle the research, and she would prepare the presentation.
note: Usually: strike a bargain with someone; strike a bargain over/on something. More formal than make a deal.

term: to come to terms with something
ru: смириться с чем-либо; принять неприятную действительность
definition: To gradually accept and learn to deal with a difficult or unpleasant situation that cannot be changed.
examples: It took him months to come to terms with losing his job.
She is still struggling to come to terms with the end of the relationship.
note: Often used with loss, failure, reality, or the fact that…; implies gradual psychological acceptance, not merely agreement.
